subject: the 4 numbers that decide every deal
preheader: cap rate, cash-on-cash, dscr, net cash flow. miss one and you're guessing.
headline: Every rental deal lives or dies on four numbers.
body: If you only run four numbers on a property, run these. Skip any of them and you're guessing.

Cap rate. NOI divided by purchase price. This is the property's grade — assumes all-cash, ignores your loan. Useful for ranking deals apples-to-apples and benchmarking against the market average. Anything more than 1.5 points above market is probably cooked.

Cash-on-cash. Annual pre-tax cash flow divided by total cash invested. This is your grade as a leveraged buyer. Cap rate tells you the property is good. Cash-on-cash tells you the deal is good. They are not the same number, and the gap between them is where leverage either helps you or kills you.

DSCR. NOI divided by annual debt service. This is the lender's gate. Below their floor (typically 1.20-1.25), the loan you modeled doesn't exist. You'll be forced to put more cash in or walk. Run this before you write the offer, not after.

Net cash flow. Rent minus PITI minus every other operating expense. This is what actually hits your bank account. Not the gross spread, not the napkin math. If net cash flow is positive and DSCR clears the lender's floor, you have a real deal. Two out of four isn't enough.
